title: introduce-kms-multi-provider-fallback-and-audit-redaction-pipeline
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds multi-provider KMS binding with geofence fallback and safe-audit redaction pipeline; requires a short rollout with policy sync. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers operating in multi-region and regulated environments frequently require both a primary KMS provider (customer-managed CMK) and a provider fallback (Redwood-managed key or alternate cloud KMS) when region-scoped keys are unavail-able or during DR. At the same time, audit logs contain potentially sensitive identifiers that must be redacted before leaving region boundaries. This PR implements a combined approach: 1) a KMS provider selection and fallback layer that respects tenant KMS bindings, geofence constraints, and an allowlist/denylist for cross-region wrapping; 2) a streaming audit-redaction pipeline that enforces configurable field-level redaction rules and provenance markers before logs are forwarded to external collectors.
Summary of changes: - Add pkg/kms/provider_router.go: provider router with policy evaluation (tenant binding, region affinity, providers priority, and DR fallback rules). - Add pkg/kms/provider_store.go: lightweight provider metadata store with caching and TTLs. - Add pkg/audit/redactor.go and pkg/audit/pipeline.go: streaming redaction stages, rules engine, and provenance header enrichment. - Add internal/rbac/policy_generator.go: small utility to synthesize RBAC v2 role bindings for the new KMS proxy service roles and audit-forwarder roles. - Add deploy/helm/templates/kms-proxy.yaml and audit-forwarder config: helm hooks to install default policies and seeding jobs. - Add migrations/20260220_kms_binding_table.sql: table to persist tenant->provider bindings and residency hints. - Tests: integration test harness in test/integration/kms_provider_fallback_test.go and unit tests for redaction rules.
Commits (high-level): - 0f7c8d9: initial provider router and interface with unit tests - 1a2b3ef: redaction pipeline + provenance headers, test harness - 9c4d2ab: RBAC generator and helm templates - d22e5b7: migration SQL and deployment config - 7b0b6a1: fix flaky test (time-dependent TTL), CI flake mitigation
Changed areas (high level): - pkg/kms/* (provider routing, policy checks) - pkg/audit/* (redaction pipeline, rule definitions) - internal/rbac/* (policy generator) - deploy/helm/templates/* (k8s manifests and seed job) - migrations/* (DB schema) - test/integration/* (integration harness)
Review conversation (abridged in-line): - Ethan Park (reviewer): "Can the provider router produce deterministic results when multiple providers have equal priority? Suggest tie-breaker by provider id and to add metrics for fallback counts." - Maya Chen (author): "Added deterministic tie-breaker (provider id) and metric kms.provider_fallback_total. Also added unit test to assert deterministic selection." - Soraya Patel: "Audit redaction rules look good, but I'm concerned about performance for high-throughput tenants. Can we ensure the pipeline is non-blocking and gives backpressure signals to the serving runtime?" - Maya Chen: "Pipeline uses lock-free ring buffer and offloads heavy regex redactions to worker pool; we added e2e perf test with 10k rps and included backpressure metrics audit.pipeline_backpressure_seconds." - Luca Romano (security approver): "Please include a migration plan for tenants with existing provider bindings; confirm rollback semantics." - Maya Chen: "Included migration script and added a rollout playbook to the PR description; rollback will re-seed previous bindings and flip a feature flag to disable fallback selection."
CI details: - CI run #4521: lint ✅, unit tests ✅, integration (k8s) initially flaky (timeout on test harness) -> rerun -> passed ✅. - Coverage: global change +0.3%. - Security scanning: dependency-check flagged transient dev dependency; upgraded and re-scanned.
Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-27 by Soraya Patel. Merge method: squash and merge.
Post-merge actions performed: - Helm seed job run in staging to populate provider binding table with test tenants - Feature flag rollout started (kms.fallback.enabled) scoped to internal accounts - Metrics dashboard added: security.KMS Fallback Rate and audit.Pipeline Backpressure - Notified infra and SRE channels about the migration window
Rollout and migration notes (what ops must do): - Run migrations on dedicated DB cluster during scheduled maintenance window (script location: migrations/20260220_kms_binding_table.sql). - Seed tenant bindings for customers that have provided CMKs using the helm job (deploy/helm/templates/kms-seed-job.yaml). - Toggle feature flag kms.fallback.enabled to gradually enable fallback behavior; observe metric kms.provider_fallback_total and audit.pipeline_backpressure_seconds. - If rollback required: disable feature flag, run rollback seeding job (deploy/helm/templates/kms-rollback-seed.yaml), and ensure no new wrapped keys are created by fallback path.
Backwards compatibility / impact: - No changes to public API surface. - Internal service-to-service auth: new service roles created via RBAC generator; operators must run the seeding job to provision role bindings in clusters using RBAC v2. - Audit exporters: consumers will receive redacted logs with a provenance.header x-rw-audit-provenance containing provider id and redaction-version.
Testing instructions: - Unit tests: run go test ./pkg/kms - Integration: run make integration-kms with local kind cluster; use test/integration/README.md for harness config. - Manual verification steps are included in deploy/helm/README.md
Post-merge follow-ups (in Linear): - ENG-8472: monitor fallback rates and adjust policy thresholds - SEC-1905: verify audit redaction rules with compliance team - OPS-312: schedule DB migration window
Summary: This PR delivers a pragmatic multi-provider KMS selection and fallback implementation together with a streaming audit redaction pipeline and supporting RBAC generator and deployment artifacts. The work is production-ready, CI green, security-reviewed, and merged to main with a controlled rollout plan and metrics to observe behavior.
